key_insight: A two-stage evolutionary hyperparameter search can make PINN training more reliable by using cheap exploratory runs to find strong configurations before fully training only the best candidates.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to reduce PINN instability and improve solution accuracy under fixed compute budgets for PDE-based scientific modeling.
method: Stage 1: run low-fidelity, truncated training to screen many hyperparameter configurations with an evolutionary algorithm.
Stage 2: fully train only the most promising candidates using standard gradient-based optimization.
Use the outer loop as a black-box search over mixed, non-differentiable PINN hyperparameters.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on Advection, Klein-Gordon, and Helmholtz problems, where it consistently outperformed standard training and achieved lower mean error under constrained computational resources.
watch_item: Because stage 1 uses truncated training, promising configurations may be misranked if early performance is not predictive of final convergence.
paper_title: Evolutionary Two-Stage Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
